questions.stem: Under NSR 2020 s. 106(1), how must a standard magnetic compass be arranged?
options: Powered from the emergency battery so that it works during a blackout
Mounted in the chart room, with a repeater at the wheel
Independent of any power supply, able to give the heading and to show it at the main steering position
Fitted with a gyro-compass repeater as its only reading
questions.explanation: A standard magnetic compass must work without any power supply and be able to show the reading at the main steering position. A compass that needs power defeats its purpose as the back-up instrument.

questions.stem: Which vessel may legally go without a standard magnetic compass?
options: A 7.5 m vessel that always navigates within sight of navigation marks
A 12 m workboat that stays within sight of navigation marks
A 7.5 m vessel that goes out of sight of navigation marks
Any vessel that carries a GNSS receiver
questions.explanation: Section 106(1)(a) excepts vessels of 8 m or less in length that navigate within sight of navigation marks (and cable ferries). Both conditions apply. Carrying GNSS does not remove the duty.

questions.stem: A Canadian vessel of 90 gross tonnage is on a domestic voyage. What does s. 106 allow for her compass fit?
options: Both a standard magnetic compass and a gyro-compass are always required
A gyro-compass alone is sufficient
A steering magnetic compass may be fitted instead of a standard magnetic compass
No compass is needed if she has a chart plotter
questions.explanation: A vessel under 150 gross tonnage may be fitted with a steering magnetic compass if she is not on an international voyage (with a gyro-compass as well if she is). A chart plotter is not a compass.

questions.stem: Where must the table or curve of residual deviations for a magnetic compass be kept?
options: Ashore, in the owner's office
On board, in the vicinity of the compass
In the engine room log
Only on the chart table, because the compass is in the wheelhouse
questions.explanation: Section 106(4) requires the compass to be properly compensated and its table or curve of residual deviations to be available on board in the vicinity of the compass.

questions.stem: At an inspection of compasses on a vessel that is not a pleasure craft, what can the master show under s. 132?
options: The most recent deviation card for each compass, signed and dated by the master and a deck officer, or a signed statement that the compasses are satisfactory
A deviation card signed by the inspector at the time of inspection
The owner's purchase receipt for each compass
A statement signed by the master alone
questions.explanation: Section 132 asks for the latest deviation card signed and dated by the master and a deck officer, or a statement signed by the master and a deck officer that the compasses have been found satisfactory. A statement signed by the master alone does not meet the wording.

questions.stem: Variation is 15 degrees E. From the open bridge wing, well clear of iron, you read 100 degrees on a hand-bearing compass to a headland. What is the true bearing?
options: 085 degrees
100 degrees
130 degrees
115 degrees
questions.explanation: A hand-bearing compass held clear of the ship's iron has variation but no deviation. Compass to true: add easterly, so 100 + 15 = 115. Subtracting (085) is the true-to-magnetic direction. 130 would add the variation twice.

questions.stem: Variation 15 degrees W, deviation on the present heading 4 degrees E. A ship's compass bearing of a tower is 210 degrees. What is the true bearing?
options: 221 degrees
199 degrees
191 degrees
229 degrees
questions.explanation: Compass error = 15 W + 4 E = 11 W. Compass to true with a westerly error: subtract, 210 - 11 = 199. 221 reverses both signs, 191 treats both as west (19 W), and 229 adds both.

questions.stem: A gyro-compass reads 214 degrees and has an error of 2 degrees W. What is the true heading?
options: 216 degrees
214 degrees
210 degrees
212 degrees
questions.explanation: A gyro has no variation or deviation, only its own error, applied like any compass error. Westerly error means the gyro reads too high, so subtract: 214 - 2 = 212. Adding (216) is the sign mistake, and 214 forgets the error.

questions.stem: You are about to take a hand-bearing compass bearing next to a steel stanchion. Which statement is correct?
options: Apply the deviation from the ship's card as well as variation
The steel does not matter because a hand compass has no deviation
Move clear of iron, or check against a known bearing first, and use variation only; the ship's deviation card does not apply to a hand compass
Add the gyro error instead
questions.explanation: Iron close to a hand compass produces errors that the ship's card does not describe. Either hold it clear of iron or check it against a known bearing. Applying the ship's deviation to a hand-held compass is a classic mistake.

questions.stem: Which of these has neither variation nor deviation, but may have an error named east or west?
options: A standard magnetic compass
A gyro-compass
A steering magnetic compass
A hand-bearing compass
questions.explanation: A gyro-compass points to true north through gyroscopic action, so magnetism is irrelevant, but it can have a gyro error that must be checked.

questions.stem: What does NSR 2020 s. 106(5) require of a vessel fitted with a magnetic compass, other than pleasure craft under 150 GT?
options: A gyro-compass as well as the magnetic compass
A spare magnetic compass of a different make
A deviation card signed by the owner
A means of correcting headings and bearings to true at all times
questions.explanation: Section 106(5) calls for a means of correcting headings and bearings to true at all times (in practice the variation, the deviation table and a way to apply them). The spare compass duty is in s. 109 for vessels of 150 GT or more.

questions.stem: Under NSR 2020 s. 145(b), a vessel required to carry charts must also be fitted with navigation accessories for what purpose?
options: To measure the speed of the current
To determine the accuracy of compass readings
To record the log book automatically
To determine the height of tide
questions.explanation: Section 145 lists accessories to permit the proper use of the charts to determine position precisely, accessories to determine the accuracy of compass readings, and binoculars.

questions.stem: Besides the log book, which record does the Master Limited chartwork competence expect you to keep?
options: A record of crew wages
A record of tide heights at each port
A record of compass errors
A record of fuel prices
questions.explanation: The draft competence statement for chartwork and pilotage includes keeping a log book and a record of compass errors.
